context.why:
US-1 built the subscription page and US-2 added the way through to the provider's billing portal. This story adds the one thing on the page that no provider's own page could ever show, because the provider does not know what your application does: what the plan a person is paying for actually gets them inside it.

The reading layer already carries this. SubscriptionReader.build_plan populates Plan.features from the features recorded against the plan's product, as a tuple of PlanFeature with an identifier and a description that falls back to the identifier. So T023 may well find that nothing is missing — the task says 'whatever the tests above show is missing', and if the tests pass on the reading as it stands, the honest outcome is a task with no production change and a note saying so. Do not invent work to fill it, and do not weaken the tests to manufacture a failure either. What the tests must prove is real: that a feature recorded against a DIFFERENT product never appears on this plan, and that a product with no features carries an empty collection rather than anything else.

The backend is drf-stripe-subscription 1.2.2, resolved at /home/sam/.cache/pypoetry/virtualenvs/django-mvp-payments-JT0CmOyG-py3.14/lib/python3.14/site-packages/drf_stripe. Read it there when you need to; never import it from mvp_payments/ or from tests/. Features live in its Feature model (feature_id primary key, nullable description) joined to products through ProductFeature. A project records them by putting space-delimited feature ids in the Stripe product's metadata, so a project that records none is normal and its page is still correct.

Documentation: docs/subscription-page.md is this feature's page and already documents PlanFeature and Plan.features. Make it true for what you add — the features component and its attributes, and anything about how a project records features that a reader would need. The documentation check reads the pages; a docstring and a changelog entry count for nothing.

prior_decisions: D1 - What counts as current is read from the backend's own property, never from a status list of ours. Nothing in this story names a status.

Decisions.md 'Why features come from the plan rather than from the person' - the backend can also answer 'every feature this person has access to' across all their current subscriptions, and that answer is the WRONG one to print beside a plan's name: somebody holding two subscriptions would read the combined list under the first plan and conclude that plan grants all of it. Features are listed per plan, from the plan's own product. Do not relitigate this.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given a product with features recorded against it, when a plan for one of its prices is read, then it carries those features; given a feature with a description, then the description is carried; given a feature with none, then the identifier is carried in its place; given a product with no features, then the plan carries an empty collection; given a feature recorded against a different product, then it never appears on this plan.

Given features, when the component renders, then it lists them, showing a description where there is one and the identifier where there is not; given none, then it renders nothing at all - no heading and no empty list.

Given the tests in T021, when they run against the reading layer as it stands, then anything they show missing is added. If nothing is missing, the task changes no production code and the report says so plainly.
Given a plan with features, when the subscription page renders, then its features appear beneath the plan they belong to; given a plan with none, then no heading and no empty list appear for it.
